Guidance

River Thames: restrictions and closures

Navigation on the River Thames may be restricted or closed in certain areas. Find out where and when these restrictions and closures are.

From:
Environment Agency
Published:
12 February 2020
Last updated:
30 August 2026 — See all updates

Contents

  1. Navigation issues: updated 26 August 2026
  2. River closures: updated 28 August 2026
  3. River restrictions: updated 28 August 2026
  4. Planned lock closures: updated 1 April 2026
  5. Contact the Environment Agency

Before boating on the River Thames, you should check the current river conditions.

For guidance on Environment Agency moorings, locks and their facilities, you should visit locks and facilities.

Navigation issues: updated 26 August 2026

When Where What’s happening
Until further notice Canal Bridge, Radcot A vehicle has damaged Canal Bridge, where Radcot Road A4095 crosses the River Thames. Please be cautious of falling debris if navigating near the bridge.
3 May 2026 until further notice Godstow Lock Shoal reported downstream of lock. Boaters should navigate with caution.
Until further notice Botley Road Bridge, Oxford Obstruction to navigation 50 metres upstream of Botley Bridge. Boaters should navigate with extreme caution.
3 February 2025 until further notice Osney reach East Street moorings, Oxford, are closed for public safety purposes, both waterside and landside. No alternative moorings are available.
1 June 2026 until further notice Abingdon reach Shoal reported downstream of lock. Boaters to navigate with caution. Shoal marked with navigation buoys.
Until further notice Clifton weir stream Shoal reported downstream of The Plough public house. Boaters are advised not to navigate up Clifton weir stream.
22 June 2024 until further notice Benson Lock Shoal reported downstream of lock. When navigating upstream the shoal is on the right hand side of the navigation channel. Boaters should navigate with caution when entering or exiting the tail gates.
18 May until further notice Benson reach Submerged vessel reported opposite Rush Court Care Home on right side of channel looking upstream. Hazard is marked with navigation buoys. Boaters should navigate with extreme caution.
20 April 2024 Until further notice Whitchurch head lock cut Obstruction to navigation above head gates. Boaters should navigate with caution when entering or exiting the upstream lock cut.
26 August until further notice Whitchurch Lock Desilting works taking place at Whitchurch Lock, boaters to be aware of delays to navigation whilst works ongoing.
23 April 2024 until further notice Caversham reach Submerged boat tied to left hand bank looking upstream, just upstream of St Mary’s Island. Boaters should navigate with caution.
5 March 2026 until further notice Caversham reach Fallen tree obstructing navigation at Poplar Island, what3words///employ.data.waving. All vessels should navigate with extreme caution.
1 June 2026 until further notice Shiplake reach Tree obstruction to navigation on Phillimore Island, right hand side of channel looking upstream. Boaters to navigate with caution. Obstruction marked with navigation buoys.
24 January 2026 until further notice Hurley Lock Vessels navigating in the weir stream towards Hurley Weir should exercise extreme caution. Unsecured chain from Harleyford Manor chain ferry potentially impacting over half of the navigation channel.
Until further notice Boulters Lock Gates on the pedestal side do not open fully. Width of the tail gates is restricted to no more than 4.8 metres (15’8). Please use caution when entering and exiting the lock.
9 February 2026 until further notice Bell Weir reach To facilitate Bell Weir refurbishment, contractors will be setting up equipment around Runnymede Pleasure Grounds. Boaters to maintain lookout for ad hoc restrictions and closures to navigation channel and navigate with caution in Bell Weir reach.
Thursday 20 August 2026 until further notice Sunbury Lock to Teddington Lock Confirmed presence of blue-green algae bloom between Sunbury Lock and Teddington Lock. Some blue-green algae can produce toxins that may be harmful to people and animals. Skin contact can cause rashes and swallowing the water can cause illness. You can find more information on the risks and the actions you can take via Algal blooms: advice for the public and landowners.
1 October 2023 until further notice Teddington Launch Lock Lock is closed for repairs to lock walls, gate ram trench and areas of the lock side. Teddington Barge Lock is fully operational.
Wednesday 29 July to Friday 11 September 2026 Teddington Lock To facilitate Teddington Launch Lock refurbishment works, contractors will be assembling equipment at the tail of the barge lock. Boaters may experience delays to navigation through the barge lock of up to 30 minutes during weekdays on the stated dates.

Planned lock closures: updated 1 April 2026

The Environment Agency carries out a programme of works on the River Thames every year between October and the end of March. This results in the closure of a number of locks sometimes for relatively long periods.

The first issue of the programme is published 10 weeks in advance of the first planned lock closure. This is so that river users can plan their winter cruising and boat movements well in advance

This programme of work is subject to change, due to weather and other circumstances. To stay updated with any changes to the programme, please subscribe to updates by selecting ‘get emails about this page’.

To receive the first issue of the programme via email, including a list of other major works, subscribe to our email subscriber list. To subscribe to or unsubscribe from this service, email riverthames@environment-agency.gov.uk with ‘subscribe’ or ‘unsubscribe’ in the subject line.

We will use your personal information in line with our privacy notice.
